hero.subtitle: When care at a Palo Alto clinic or hospital goes wrong, the aftermath can leave you with more questions than answers. We handle medical malpractice claims under California's MICRA rules and can review your situation at no cost.

about.title: Palo Alto Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Palo Alto is home to major medical centers and a dense network of clinics and specialists serving Santa Clara County residents. With that concentration of care comes a steady stream of patients who trust their providers to catch problems, communicate clearly, and follow through on treatment plans. When that trust breaks down — through a delayed diagnosis, a surgical slip, or a medication mix-up — the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law sets a high bar for these claims: MICRA requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in, strict notice deadlines apply, and a bad result by itself isn't proof of malpractice. We listen to what happened, evaluate your situation, and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Palo Alto Patients Choose Us

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the injury and no more than three years from the date it happened, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Required — We Help You Find It
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in on a malpractice claim, we know how to line up that kind of review early.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, Ever
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. That's true whether your case involves a Palo Alto clinic, a specialist's office, or a larger hospital system.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't prove malpractice occurred. We typically need a qualified medical expert to review the care and determine whether it fell below the accepted standard.

items.question: How much time do I have to file a claim in Palo Alto?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement, so it's worth having a claim reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it matter that Palo Alto has several large medical institutions nearby?
items.answer: It can affect how a case is investigated, since larger institutions often have their own internal review and record-keeping processes. Our team is familiar with these systems and can help figure out what records to request and how to proceed.

items.question: What do you do?
items.answer: We handle medical malpractice claims and listen to your situation. If it's something we can help with, we'll evaluate your case under California law and explain your options.
